history.new: J. Brox, ETP Zulip, Jan 12, 2025: 'There are no models whatsoever of 677 in size 10 (39h in Mace4)' (topic 'FINITE: 677 -> 255', https://leanprover-community.github.io/archive/stream/458659-Equational/topic/FINITE.3A.20677.20-.3E.20255.html); R. Schneider reported a complete general model search up to n = 11 (Nov 21, 2025, same topic). So the orders <= 10 of 677 (1, 5, 7, 9) were known; the lab adds the first independently checkable certificate (DRAT proofs verified by drat-trim, re-derived by the Skeptic with another encoding) (Historian spectrum audit 2026-10-20, reviews/historian_spectra_2026.md).
history.old: Low confidence. Not stated in the sources read: the ETP paper (arXiv:2512.07087) reports Mace4 exhausting size 8 (section 7.3.1) and gives exhaustion times for 'certain special E677 models' of sizes 9-19 (Table 4) without defining them; the ETP blueprint chapter on equation 677 (https://teorth.github.io/equational_theories/blueprint/677-chapter.html) has no size results; B. Le Floch's notes give no sizes for 677. The ETP's dedicated EQ677 model searcher and its model database (manual on the Lean Zulip, 2026) may well settle order 10 already. Mainly a certified data point for the open finite implication 677 => 255: there is no counterexample of order 8 or 10.

statement: No magma of order 10 satisfies x = y(x((yx)y)) (ETP equation 677). With CLM-C05-07, CLM-C05-08, CLM-C05-11 and the ETP notes, the orders n <= 10 of finite models of 677 are exactly 1, 5, 7 and 9.
title: Law 677 has no model of order 10 (DRAT-certified); its orders up to 10 are exactly 1, 5, 7, 9
